thread:
oncall-bot: Pager: HIGH - gpu-pool-prod-eu capacity critical. queue_depth ~125k, tail latency spiking, autoscaler hit max_replicas=50. Multiple nodes reporting driver OOM + CUDA/Xid errors.
alex: ack. I'm on it. @sara @kai can you grab runtime + autoscaler logs? I'll notify CS about possible customer impact.
kai: looking. Autoscaler pushed to 50 but cloud quotas block further node launches. We see API errors: `QuotaExceeded::InsufficientAcceleratorQuota`. Autoscaler retries every 20s, then backoff. No scale-ins happening yet.
sara: runtime note: seeing repeated kernel OOMs and Xid 78 on 6 nodes (driver 530.101). dmesg shows NVML reset and processes getting killed. Suspect a bad driver patch last night on pool-update. Logs:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 78, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568012] nvidia: GPU watchdog timeout
[ 1234.569100] oom-killer: Killed process 18237 (beam_worker) total-vm: 10240000kB
```
alex: ok — two parallel mitigations: 1) stop autoscaler from spinning useless retries (temporarily put to manual) 2) reduce incoming load and route low-priority batches to a backup CPU pool.
alex: @kai can you flip autoscaler to manual and set replicas=50 stable? show command you used.
kai: ran: `redwoodctl autoscaler update --pool gpu-prod-eu --mode manual --replicas 50` — autoscaler paused. Also created cloud support ticket for accel quota bump.
ops-bot: automation: started drain on nodes [gpu-eu-12,gpu-eu-18] flagged with driver 530.101.
dave: manual rebooting gpu-eu-18 now (soft reboot) to try driver reload. ETA ~2m.
maria: CS update: we have ~12 customer tickets reporting 502s and chatops alerts. Some bigger customers report multi-minute tail latencies. Sharing status page note in 5.
alex: immediate config change: throttle batch size for `large-gen` route to 1 and reduce concurrency from 8->2. Command:
```
redwoodctl route update --route large-gen --batch-size 1 --concurrency 2
```
kai: applied. That should reduce GPU OOM pressure from huge batches.
sara: confirmed kernel OOMs stopped on nodes that were rebooted, driver still flaky on 4 nodes. Suggest rolling pool back to driver 525.* until driver team vets 530.101. Rollback plan:
- cordon bad nodes
- drain workloads
- reprovision with driver 525 image
Commands I will run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-eu-12
kubectl drain gpu-eu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
image-builder reprovision --node gpu-eu-12 --driver 525.85
```
alex: good. Meanwhile ops, can we spin up ephemeral CPU workers for low-priority async workloads? we should avoid dropping customer jobs.
ops-bot: spun up 12 cpu-backed workers in pool `cpu-async-eu`. Routing rule created to send `priority=low` async tasks there.
dave: gpu-eu-18 back online, driver reloaded, no Xid in last 30s. Still seeing one node with repeated Xid 35.
maria: published incident notice on status: "Partial degradation for generation endpoints in EU region. Mitigation in progress."
alex: estimate customer impact: increased latencies for ~8% of requests, ~3% error rate for heavy batch routes. CS to keep customers updated.
kai: cloud ticket created (CLOUD-7892) for GPU quota. Requested temporary quota increase to 70 nodes. Pending approval.
sara: rolling driver rollback in progress. I'll update when node 4/6 reprovisioned.
ops-bot: automation: 4 nodes reprovisioned with driver 525.85, workloads rescheduled.
dave: after rollback, aggregate queue depth dropped from 125k -> 40k in 18m. Good sign.
alex: nice. Next steps: 1) keep autoscaler manual until quota confirmed 2) monitor driver telemetry for 24h 3) create postmortem draft with timeline and suggested release gating for driver updates.
maria: CS: will send pre-approved customer note and include ETA for full recovery ~2h.
sara: logging note: we need to add driver-version as a tag on future pod logs to speed investigations. Filing infra ticket.
alex: handing off at 22:00UTC to night on-call @dave. Summary in #incidents pinned. If any spike, page ops oncall.
oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place, partial recovery. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
